: Watch this leading Kalamkari artist use a finely pointed ‘kalam,’ or pen made from a bamboo stick, to delicately outline traditional Indian patterns and motifs onto cloth.
Originating from the Indian states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, Kalamkari is a traditional art form of hand-painting or block-printing onto cloth and derives its name from the word ‘kalam,’ which means pen. Only natural dyes are used in Kalamkari, in a process that involves 23 meticulous steps. Browse original Kalamkari paintings online at or visit Laasya Art gallery in Palo Alto (San Francisco Bay Area).
